tasks.task: Turn a thin request into a brief, budget and timeline

items.when: When an event is agreed with a date or date range and you need the steps to doors open
When the request is thin and you need purpose, success measure, guest count and a full budget
When the budget could buy two kinds of event, to compare two plans with money and dates
When the event risks being forgettable, to plan the one peak worth building, with owners and costs
When guests pay, to set ticket prices, early-bird terms and how seats and dates are shown
When the plan is a list of logistics, to walk through each scene as a guest and find what drags
When the brief is drafted, to have a fresh reviewer read it as the person paying for the event

tasks.task: Write the run sheet and the if-this-goes-wrong plan

items.when: When the day needs every line timed, placed and owned, with a cue and a backup
When one backup per line is not enough, to model several things going wrong at once
When radios or phones may fail, to set fallback ways to reach the crew and who switches
When suppliers hand over to each other, to check each join and what gives way in a clash
When the sheet assumes nobody slips, to check handoffs, warnings and human mistakes

tasks.task: Brief venues and suppliers and compare their quotes

items.when: When you need comparable quotes from caterers, AV, venues, furniture, security or printers
When quotes come back and must be compared like for like before anyone signs
When the quotes must sit side by side in one table first
When deposits and lead times differ, to compare risk and how safe each deposit is
When two or three venues are close, to have a fresh reviewer pick one against the brief

tasks.task: Summarise a venue or supplier contract on one page

items.when: When a contract arrives and you need its dates, minimums, cancellation terms and duties
When you want a second plain reading of what each side owes, to compare
When attrition, cancellation or damage terms look one-sided, to flag them for a lawyer

tasks.task: Write invitations, reminders and the day-before email

items.when: Once the date, venue and programme are fixed
When the reminders all say the same thing, to compare three plans for the series
Before sending, to check a guest can register from the link today
Before sending, to have a fresh reviewer read each email as a guest who knows nothing

tasks.task: Design the registration form and the attendee data plan

items.when: Before registration opens, or when a form asks for more than it needs
When the form is long, to try a staged version with conditional questions
When people start the form and drop out, to cut fields and clear up the wording
When the form collects dietary, access or health details, to list the privacy risks
When the form is live, to check a guest can complete it today

tasks.task: Build the access and inclusion checklist

items.when: When choosing a venue, and again two weeks before the event
When guests have access needs, to plan step-free routes and what the venue must confirm
When first-time visitors must find the way, to map each point where they choose a route
When the plan fits a typical guest, to ask who cannot take part and offer more than one way in

tasks.task: Plan promotion to fill the room

items.when: When you know the event type and goal and need a plan to fill seats and follow up
When the event must be announced across platforms, with posts made for each
When the event is a launch, to time channels and announcement copy around the day
When money is tight, to compare a paid push with an invite-led one, with costs and dates

tasks.task: Make the event page

items.when: When the event needs a page with a plan, copy and firm design rules
When the first screen must sell the event, to see three made as real pages and one chosen
Before the page goes live, to check every date, time, speaker and price against the brief
When the page is live, to check a visitor can book a place today

tasks.task: Shape the programme and the opening remarks

items.when: When there are too many sessions, to cut to the best few in an order that holds attention
When a keynote buries its point, to reorder it so the room knows the stakes early
When the host needs a two-minute timed opening with one story and a close
When the running order sags, to strengthen the core and cut weak material

tasks.task: Plan event signs, posters and printed pieces

items.when: Before any layout, to find the one idea and one symbol the poster or banner should carry
When you need what each sign says and where it stands at every decision point
When you have the event details and want a guided run to a layout and an export checklist
When the look is undecided, to see three directions made at real size and one chosen
When there are no usable photos, to try a type-only poster that reads from far away
When a layout is drafted, to see where the eye lands first and what to cut
When the client's team will build and reprint the pieces themselves

tasks.task: Brief crew and volunteers and set the day rota

items.when: When each crew member needs the lines they own pulled from the run sheet
When the day needs cover at busy hours within the staff you have
When volunteers are new, to get an induction procedure and a practice plan
When volunteers need clear roles, screening, training and shift plans

tasks.task: Check the catering order before service

items.when: When the order must match the minimums and deadlines in the caterer's contract
Before the day, to check the order against the quote and event details and list mismatches
When numbers or dietary needs change late, to check each change against the confirmed order

tasks.task: Shortlist shows and plan the trade show year

items.when: Once a year to choose shows, then for each show from three months before to 30 days after
When shows and packages must be ranked on audience fit, full cost and cost per qualified lead
When the firm has never exhibited, to frame one show as a small test with decision rules
When a show is booked from habit, to ask what the organiser gains and what you really get

tasks.task: Plan the booth and the staff kit

items.when: When a show is booked and you need the stand plan, goals, staff roles and lead capture
When staff need a short demo that explains the product and lets the visitor see the result
When the stand needs a one-pager and an objection sheet for staff
When the stand graphics are undecided, to see three directions made at real size
When the kit is drafted, to have a fresh reviewer read it as a visitor walking past

tasks.task: Decide whether a sponsorship or exhibitor package is worth it

items.when: When an organiser offers a package and the client wants go, negotiate or walk away
When you want a second view with a cost comparison and a small capped pilot
When the offer flatters the brand, to turn it upside down and check incentives

tasks.task: Build sponsor packages for your own event

items.when: When your event needs sponsor tiers, pitch copy and a list of promises to track
When the sponsor pitch needs an outline that builds belief and ends in a clear ask
When there are two or three tier structures, to have a fresh reviewer pick one

tasks.task: Follow up guests and leads after the event

items.when: The day after any event, show or webinar, to run the wrap-up in order
When attendance, lead notes and costs are to hand and thank-yous and follow-ups must go
When follow-ups should be grouped by what each person asked for at the event
When the show gave many leads, to score them on fit and activity and rank who gets a call
When the follow-up is a series, to compare three plans, each with its first email
When a speaker, sponsor or helper deserves one short, specific thank-you with no ask
Before sending, to have a fresh reviewer read the emails as a guest or a lead

tasks.task: Write the results report and check budget against actual

items.when: When the numbers are in and the client needs results against the success measure
When actual costs differ from the budget, to say what moved and why
When guest feedback has come in from several places, to rank what guests really need
When the team will run this event again, to note what to repeat and what to change

tasks.task: Plan a webinar or an online event

items.when: When the webinar must teach one clear result, to get an outline, a deck brief and promotion
When you have the topic and audience and need a plan to promote, run and follow up
After the session, to turn the recording into posts, emails and clips

tasks.task: Plan an offsite, a tasting or a fundraising event

items.when: When a team meets off site and needs a decision-first agenda and a pre-read request
When the event must raise money, to get a budget, income scenarios and a day schedule
When the event lets buyers try product versions, to plan the day and a decision rule

tasks.task: Brief the photographer and plan posts around the event

items.when: When a photographer or video team needs one clear brief for the day
When the event needs before, during and after posts for each platform

always.when: Before any invitation, run sheet or sign goes out, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When signs, posters, badges or stand graphics must be laid out as print-ready artwork
When the event must sell sponsor packages and manage what each sponsor was promised
When invitations go to a large list and need segments, timing and delivery checks
When the event needs a full site or booking page built, not only its copy
When show leads must be logged, routed and chased through to a quote
When the event needs daily posting and replies before, during and after

gaps: No library item writes a run sheet or cue sheet for an event day; only the kit skill does
No library item builds a general event budget; the one that exists is for nonprofit fundraisers
No library item shortlists venues, compares them or gives a site-visit checklist
No library item writes event invitations and reminder emails
No library item finds speakers, writes a speaker brief or scripts a host for the whole day
No library item plans a trade show stand layout or a lead capture form with scoring
No library item writes an event risk assessment covering crowds, weather, fire and first aid
No library item designs an attendee feedback survey
No library item plans group travel, room blocks and transfers
No library item makes a seating plan, a floor plan or name badges
